newsitem.title: GERMANY: Caterpillar buys Krupp diesel motor unit.
newsitem.headline: Caterpillar buys Krupp diesel motor unit.

text.p: Earth-moving equipment manufacturer Caterpillar Inc. said Monday it would pay an undisclosed amount for the MaK diesel motor unit of German steel maker Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp.
Caterpillar plans to keep all 1,500 MaK employees and run the unit as a an independent Kiel-based business called MaK Motoren GmbH, the company said.

MaK, a producer of ship engines and other medium-sized motors, would compliment Caterpillar's existing lines of heavy equipment, truck, and generator motors. It had 1995 sales of 541 million German marks ($349 million).

"MaK has excellent growth potential," said Donald Western, the head of Caterpillar's motor business. "Caterpillar can offerthe finances and resources to help MaK with new products, new markets and new technologies."
Caterpillar's motor business provided about a quarter of its $16 billion in sales in 1995.

Western said Caterpillar may pursue other takeovers as part of its growth strategy. "MaK fits into our concept of making acquisitions with above-average growth potenial in our core segments," he said.
